title: Streaming token-flow shepherd: adaptive PR gating for p95/tokens-sec regressions
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, streaming performance harness that runs as part of PR checks and detects meaningful p95 and tokens/sec regressions with low false-positive rate. This ticket implements an adaptive baseline that ages based on recent commits and production traffic shape so regression gates stay relevant for models with drifting sequence-length distributions. Deliverables: (1) a PR workflow step that runs a short microbenchmark against the PR build; (2) an adaptive baseline service that returns expected p95 and token/sec bands per-model and per-sequence-length bucket; (3) a gating decision engine that emits pass/warn/fail with an explainable rationale and links to artifacts.
background: Current CI gates either run heavy replay baselines (long runtime) or rely on static snapshots that become stale when model code, quantization, or serving kernels change. This forces long PR cycles or noisy failures. We need a middle ground: a streaming, short-duration microbench that is sensitive to meaningful regressions but robust to noisy fluctuations caused by transient infra variability.
proposal_summary: Implement a streaming microbench harness that issues synthetic variable-length requests representative of workload slices (short/med/long). Use exponentially-weighted moving averages (EWMA) for per-slice baselines with confidence bands computed from historical variance and run-to-run jitter. Gate logic: if PR median p95 exceeds baseline p95 + adaptive_margin (function of baseline sigma and sample size) then fail; if within margin but trending worse, mark warn. Provide automatic artifact uploads (bench traces, perf flame, tokens/sec time series) and post a structured comment on the PR linking to results.
acceptance_criteria: CI step runs in <12 minutes for 16-sample microbench on standard runner
False-positive rate <= 3% measured on historical PRs (sample of 200 past merges)
Detects injected regression of 12% p95 slowdown with >=95% recall in synthetic canary runs
Adaptive baseline service exposes per-model, per-length-bucket bands and an API used by the PR step
PR comment includes: pass/warn/fail, p95 delta, tokens/sec delta, link to raw artifacts (S3/bench dashboard), and recommended rollback model/version if applicable
Docs updated: runbook for triaging fail/warn (run full replay, compare kernel logs, check KV cache hit rates)
implementation_steps: Spike: implement microbench harness that can emit variable-length traces and collect p50,p95,tokens/sec (2d)
Service: build a lightweight baseline service (Go) with EWMA per-slice baseline and retention/decay policy (3d)
CI integration: add GitHub Actions step that deploys PR build to ephemeral infra and runs harness, uploads artifacts (4d)
Gate logic: implement pass/warn/fail policy and threshold tuning UI in Redwood Console (2d)
Rollout: alpha to internal dev-only by toggled config, run on 100 PRs and measure FPR/recall (2w)
Hardening: add retry and noise-suppression (outlier trimming), integrate with alerting and perf regressions dashboard (3d)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Short microbench may miss regressions that only appear under sustained throughput — mitigate by scheduling nightly full replays as complement
Adaptive baseline can be tuned too aggressively and hide real regressions if decay is too fast — use conservative decay and require longer term trend before auto-suppressing an alert
Ephemeral infra variability (runner warmup, noisy neighbors) can create noise — use repeated samples, warmup iterations, and trimmed mean for stability
metrics_to_track: False positive rate on historical PRs
Mean delta in p95 and tokens/sec for gated PRs
Number of manual triages triggered per month
observability_and_artifacts: Upload raw per-request latency traces to s3://redwood-perf/eng/ENG-63421/{pr}/{run}
Automatic flamegraphs for slow tokens and kernel selection traces
Link to baseline service metrics (Prometheus) and decay windows
testing_plan: Unit tests for gate logic and baseline decay math
Integration tests in CI using a known good model and an artificially slowed model (inject 15% sleep)
Backtest across last 200 merged PRs to compute expected FPR and tweak margins
Chaos test: run harness with injected runner noise to validate outlier trimming
docs_and_communication: Announce alpha in #perf and schedule demo for platform and SRE teams
Add Console help-text for gate results and triage checklist
